title: Monash rejects Centuria data centre plans as Victoria tightens planning rules
key_facts: Monash Council in Melbourne rejected Centuria's AU$137 million, 38 MW data centre at 1816-1832 Dandenong Road, Clayton, on 29 Sep 2026.
Council planning officers had recommended approval and found noise and 80-metre home separation acceptable.
Councillors cited scale, electricity needs and impact on neighbours, and Victoria's new Sustainable Data Centre Action Plan.
The plan proposes a 150-metre separation from homes and expects new data centres to bring their own renewable energy; the new rules are not yet in force and would start in early 2027.
Centuria has a second application for up to 40 MW on the same site; it may be able to challenge the refusal.
Mayor Stuart James said he did not know how successful a refusal would be.
quote_evidence: Monash Council has rejected Centuria’s plans for a 38MW data centre in Melbourne, overturning a recommendation by council planning officers to approve the AU$137 million project as the state of Victoria moves to tighten rules governing where and how data centres can be built.
The new requirements are not yet in force, however, and Paterson’s motion rested on the scale, intensity and operational nature of the development as opposed to the 150-metre rule.
why_it_matters_hint: A council refused a project that its own officers backed, as Victoria rewrites data centre rules.
notes: W.Media says it asked Centuria about its options; no reply reported.
